content:
Hi!

I'll be reading through Mark Wilde's Quantum Information Theory soon, and was hoping to make contributions formalizing results from it in Physlib's QuantumInfo part, if that's still of interest.

I was trying to figure out the current state of the Wilde-book TODO list. The link to it from the Physlib GitHub repo seems to be stale (404s), and it looks like physlib.io/todo doesn't cover it either, since that page is auto-generated from tags already in the code. The old Lean-QuantumInfo repo (merged into Physlib) still has its TODO.md up though: https://github.com/Timeroot/Lean-QuantumInfo/blob/main/TODO.md

A few questions:
Is formalizing more of Wilde's book still an active goal for the project, or has focus shifted elsewhere since the Stein's Lemma work wrapped up?

And is that old TODO.md still roughly accurate as a map of what's formalized vs. not from the book, or has it drifted since the merge?

If it's still of interest to formalize more of the book, I'd be happy to contribute :)

I can't speak to the specifics of this question, so will leave that to others. But I can say something generally:

The unformalised results from Wilde's book will still be of use to formalise, and a good way to extend the Quantum-Info API. So if this is something you want to do, it is a worth-while task!

On a side note there is an ongoing task of merging the ./QuantumInfo part into ./Physlib, and we are looking for people to start this effort in earnest. A useful side-quest might be to move the parts from Wilde which have already been formalised from ./QuantumInfo to ./Physlib (with the associated cleaning up etc.).
